text:
[RDSC.9.9] **A `.dsc` is trusted input.** An integration loads an artefact
deliberately, and the artefact's provenance is the integration's responsibility,
not the runtime's. Whether an artefact was built to attack a runtime is not a
question a load can decide, so a runtime **must not** spend load time, or memory,
analysing an artefact for malicious construction.

A loader **may** refuse an artefact for compatibility — the version series
([LDET.1.10]) — or for a cheap structural need of its own ([RDSC.4a.9.1]). It **must not** refuse
or analyse an artefact on the ground that it may be hostile. Heavier verification
of an artefact belongs to a separate tool that runs when someone chooses to run
it, never as part of a load.

**A program a trace embeds ([RFCS.13]) is trusted the same way**: whoever opens
the trace chooses to run it.

**So are a recorded fact stream ([RFCS.1]) and a `FactExternal` ([NCBK.10.4]).**
Whoever opens a trace chooses to replay it, and an
integration chooses the tiers it takes a `FactExternal` from. The integration
**must** accept either only from a source it trusts. A reader of either **may**
refuse it for compatibility or for a cheap structural need of its own, and
**must not** refuse or analyse it on the ground that it may be hostile, as a
loader must not.

**Trust does not extend to corrupting the host.** Whatever bytes it is handed, a
loader **must** either load them or refuse them, and an engine running what it
loaded **must** fault rather than read or write outside what it allocated. This
is a property of the code that reads the bytes, not an analysis of the artefact,
and it costs no load pass of its own. A fact-stream reader owes the same for
every stream it reads, and `ds_engine_assert_external` for every record it is
handed: a record that breaks a refusal of [NCBK.10.4] is refused, whatever its
bytes.

This clause covers the `.dsc`, embedded or not, a recorded fact stream and a
`FactExternal`. Adapter data and every other host input come from outside the
deployment, and the clauses that defend against them stand.

---
gap_reason: The first half is an obligation of absence: a runtime does no load-time analysis for malicious construction, and no vector can show that a check is missing. The second half, that no bytes corrupt the host, is a property over all inputs, which the `fuzz-dsc` lane measures for the loader. A fuzzer is not a conformance test.
